The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly
Why, in plain words: A configuration change gave the shop a cache address that refused its connections, so every account page had to be worked out from scratch: the pages stayed correct but got slow.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 7m 0s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #551 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly while deploy/values-production.yaml:cache.port was 6380
Incident: HighLatency on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:43 to 03:50 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:13:24 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:49:27 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 03:43 UTC and was back to normal at 03:50 UTC, 7 minutes later. What its alert watches went from 26.6 ms before it began to 191 ms at its worst. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A configuration change gave the shop a cache address that refused its connections, so every account page had to be worked out from scratch: the pages stayed correct but got slow. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #551, for a person to review and merge. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). The refused cache port, or another wrong cache address, could reach production again and slow every account page.

Impact
7m 0s - onset until back to normal
1.1% to 1.1% - error rate, before onset and while broken on average (no rise)
26.6 ms to 190 ms - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (worst minute 191 ms; the rule's line is 100 ms)
none - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The production values file had `cache.port` changed from 6379 to 6380, and the summary cache refused connections on that port. Every summary-cache lookup failed, so on every request the account page fell back to working out each shopper's spend figure from scratch. That fallback keeps pages correct but slow.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly: the slowest replica's median time to answer a request rose far above its usual level, while failed requests stayed within their normal range.
  Evidence:
    AL1 p50 latency above threshold for 5m
why 1 Pages were slow because the account page could not use its rendered-summary cache. Its configuration says that when the cache cannot be reached, the page works out the shopper's spend figure from scratch, and the logs show that happening on every request.
  Evidence:
    S1 deploy/values-production.yaml at 0d8e826
    Gd3f7 ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 03:42–03:49; # was 50 to 200, typically 200, highest at 03:43
why 2 The cache could not be used because every lookup was refused: the service connected to the cache on port 6380, and the cache refused the connection. As read at 03:49:51 UTC, all replicas ran revision 0d8e826, whose configuration sets that port.
  Evidence:
    Gd3f7
    S1
    T13 03:49:51 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 0d8e826, deployed at 03:42:44
why 3 The service pointed at that port because the deploy of revision 0d8e826 at 03:42:44 UTC changed the cache port in deploy/values-production.yaml from 6379 to 6380, a port on which the cache refused connections.
  Evidence:
    P2 03:42:44 UTC deploy 0d8e826 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 0d8e826 to io-shop, compared against 544cef3 - the revision deployed before it.
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 544cef3 at Nov 10, 23:42:44 UTC: the metrics read show the service healthy with it in place until the onset at 03:43 UTC.
      T4 03:49:37 Investigator Agent: Read back 360 minutes of metrics
      T5 03:49:38 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 03:43
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:49:51.
      T16
    A source-code change shipped in the same deploy: the diff lists only deploy/values-production.yaml, so every other file was as it was at the previous revision.
      D1
Contributing factors
- No check was seen, in review or before the deploy, that the cache address in the deployment configuration accepts connections. A change to the cache port shipped to production unchallenged. (AI-4)
- The deploy reached every replica, and no gate was seen that watches latency or cache-lookup failures after rollout to halt or reverse it. (AI-5)
- No alert on summary-cache lookup failures was seen. The fault was found only by the latency alert, although connection-refused errors were logged from the first minute. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The deploy of revision 0d8e826 at 03:42:44 UTC changed cache.port in deploy/values-production.yaml from 6379 to 6380. The summary cache refuses connections on 6380, so cache_hit_ratio fell to 0 and p50 latency rose from about 26ms to about 190ms. The cache itself is healthy and the source code is unchanged. | 0.93 | confirmed

Trigger
deploy/values-production.yaml:cache.port went from 6379 to 6380 at 03:42:44 UTC, in the deploy of 0d8e826 that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:49:58 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 03:53:45 | Proposed a fix: PR #551 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 03:43 UTC. HighLatency fired at 03:49:02 UTC, 6 minutes 2 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | p50 latency above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #551 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a pre-deploy check, in CI or at sync, that for every change to io-shop's deployment values confirms the configured cache host and port accept connections from the target environment, and blocks the deploy if they do not. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Roll io-shop deploys out progressively, with automated analysis that halts and rolls back the rollout when latency or summary-cache lookup failures rise on the first replicas. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Add an alert on io-shop summary-cache lookup failures (connection refused or unreachable). | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Route the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that it pages a person. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 48 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 0d8e826 changed.
- 50 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:49:51.
- 56 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 2 minutes 4 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 43 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #551.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the HighLatency alert on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort
none - engineer time
232,207 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/475c19d2-5b4c-4b60-b8de-b10a94c5e33c

Changes to production read
P1 | Nov 10, 2026, 23:42:44 UTC deploy 544cef3 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
P2 | 03:42:44 UTC deploy 0d8e826 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory

Log messages read (UTC)

Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 37 minutes, 03:13–03:49; # was 0.50% to 2.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 03:26
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 4 occurrences in 22 minutes, 03:18–03:39
Gd3f7 | ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 03:42–03:49; # was 50 to 200, typically 200, highest at 03:43
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 0d8e826 to io-shop, compared against 544cef3 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -22,4 +22,4 @@ resources:
   # address is right.
   cache:
     host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
  -  port: 6379
  +  port: 6380
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | What was wrong: deploy/values-production.yaml sets cache.port: 6380. The investigation's evidence shows every summary cache lookup in production failing with "connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380", and the investigation says the cache itself is healthy. 6379 was the port before the deploy and is the one the cache serves on. The wrong value is in this file.

The change:
• deploy/values-production.yaml: cache.port goes from 6380 back to 6379. Nothing else in the file changes.
• New test tests/io_shop/test_deploy_values.py: reads the production values file, finds the top-level cache: block by parsing lines (so it adds no YAML dependency), and checks that port is 6379 and host is cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local.

What the test is for: The port check is written to fail against the file as it stands (6380) and to pass with this change. Its job is to make a future change to the cache address show up in review and CI, not only as a fall in cache hit ratio after a deploy.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/values-production.yaml at 0d8e826
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: Shoppers using io-shop found that their account pages loaded slowly for {duration}. A configuration change pointed the shop at a cache address that refused its connections, so account pages had to be built from scratch every time they were requested. The pages still showed the right information, but they took longer to appear. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in lost takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one, so no responders were called in. Argus ended the incident by rolling back the io-shop deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a permanent fix, which is open as a draft pull request and has not yet been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
